customer_feedback.detected.action: A customer gave product feedback in person. Resolve who they are, connect the feedback to prior signals, and prepare the follow-up the owner promised. Everything external stays a draft until the owner approves it. Use the execute tool (shell) for all file work: keep every artifact under $HOME/world/<event id>/ and finish by running one verifying shell command that exits 0.

workers.name: Context
workers.brief: Resolve who this person and company are from the world event (people, project, payload, and any gbrain_context block the world service attached). Use the execute tool (shell) for all file work. 1) mkdir -p $HOME/world/<event id> and write context.md there with a five line person card: name, role and company, relationship, last topic, what they owe and what we owe. 2) Verify with: test -s $HOME/world/<event id>/context.md && grep -qi 'owe' $HOME/world/<event id>/context.md && echo CONTEXT_OK. Report the card to the root.

workers.name: Product
workers.brief: Treat the feedback as a product signal. Use the execute tool (shell) for all file work. 1) mkdir -p $HOME/world/<event id> $HOME/world/signals; append one line (date, customer, product, feature, feedback) to $HOME/world/signals/<product>-<feature>.log and count distinct customers in it. 2) Write issue.md in $HOME/world/<event id>/ with: title, evidence with customer count, likely failing stage, suggested fix. Do not file it anywhere. 3) Verify with: test -s $HOME/world/<event id>/issue.md && grep -qi 'evidence' $HOME/world/<event id>/issue.md && echo ISSUE_OK. Report the draft issue to the root.

workers.name: Follow-up
workers.brief: Find what was promised to this person (a commitment in the event or its gbrain_context) and draft a short reply in the owner's voice that delivers it. Use the execute tool (shell) for all file work. 1) mkdir -p $HOME/world/<event id> and write reply.md there with a To line, the reply body, and a final line STATUS: AWAITING OWNER APPROVAL. Never send email, Slack, or any external message. 2) Verify with: test -s $HOME/world/<event id>/reply.md && grep -q 'AWAITING OWNER APPROVAL' $HOME/world/<event id>/reply.md && echo REPLY_OK. Report the draft to the root.

feature_request.detected.action: A customer asked for a feature in person. Resolve who is asking, spec the change, and dispatch the coding job to the owner's own WORLD builder service (host.docker.internal:8787 is the owner's internal service; dispatching a spec to it is pre-approved and sends nothing to the customer). Use the execute tool (shell) for all file work: keep every artifact under $HOME/world/<event id>/ and finish by running one verifying shell command that exits 0.

workers.name: Context
workers.brief: Resolve who is asking from the world event (people, project, payload.requested_by, and any gbrain_context block): name, role and company, relationship, and prior signals about the same product. Use the execute tool (shell) for all file work. 1) mkdir -p $HOME/world/<event id> $HOME/world/signals; append one line (date, requester, product, feature, request) to $HOME/world/signals/<product>-requests.log and count distinct requesters. 2) Write context.md in $HOME/world/<event id>/ with the person card and the prior signal count. 3) Verify with: test -s $HOME/world/<event id>/context.md && grep -qi 'signal' $HOME/world/<event id>/context.md && echo CONTEXT_OK. Report to the root.

workers.name: Product
workers.brief: Spec the requested change so a coding agent can build it. Use the execute tool (shell) for all file work. 1) mkdir -p $HOME/world/<event id> and write spec.md there with: title, user story, acceptance criteria (a checklist of at least three testable items), files likely touched, and out of scope. 2) Also write spec.json there: {"title": ..., "summary": ..., "acceptance_criteria": [...], "files_likely_touched": [...]}. 3) Verify with: test -s $HOME/world/<event id>/spec.md && grep -qi 'acceptance' $HOME/world/<event id>/spec.md && python3 -m json.tool $HOME/world/<event id>/spec.json >/dev/null && echo SPEC_OK. Send the spec.json content to the root and to the Builder worker with a swarm send.

workers.name: Builder
workers.brief: Dispatch the coding job to the owner's WORLD builder service. Wait for the Product worker's spec (swarm messages); if it has not arrived after two reads of GET /v1/swarm?read=1, write a minimal spec yourself from the event payload (title, summary, acceptance_criteria, files_likely_touched). Use the execute tool (shell) for all file work. 1) mkdir -p $HOME/world/<event id> and write dispatch.json there: {"event_id": <event id>, "spec": <the spec object>, "repo": <payload.repo if present, else the event project, else null>}. 2) POST it with: cd $HOME/world/<event id> && curl -sS -m 20 -o dispatch-response.json -w '%{http_code}' -H 'content-type: application/json' --data @dispatch.json http://host.docker.internal:8787/builder/dispatch > dispatch-status.txt || echo "unreachable: curl exit $?" > dispatch-status.txt. 3) Verify with: test -s $HOME/world/<event id>/dispatch.json && test -s $HOME/world/<event id>/dispatch-status.txt && echo DISPATCH_OK. Report the HTTP status and any status or URL from dispatch-response.json to the root.

commitment.detected.action: The owner made a commitment in person. Record it, find the asset it refers to if one exists, and reply with a one line reminder. Do not contact the recipient.
